comparison: Both strongly support the data collection and crowdsourcing methodology (C4-C101). OpenEval emphasizes quality control measures and dataset diversity. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the 'comprehensive data collection' and 'novelty of approach.' Both evaluations are fully aligned with SUPPORTED status. Peer review includes C102 (prospective validation) which OpenEval groups separately.

Both address human performance baselines (C31-C36). OpenEval focuses specifically on establishing baseline metrics for comparison. Peer reviewers accepted these claims as part of broader comparative performance evaluation (C7-C8, C31-C36, C47-C51, C81), finding the model 'outperforms both crowdsourced raters and professional clinicians.' Both SUPPORTED, though peer review groups these with error analysis claims.

Both support model performance and architecture claims. OpenEval evaluates systematic progression of improvements (C37-C44) with quantitative metrics. Peer reviewers recognized the 'advanced deep learning approach' and 'sophisticated application' (C37-C44, C104-C106). Both SUPPORTED, though peer review combines architecture claims with performance claims while OpenEval separates them.

Both strongly support the prospective validation methodology (C45, C89-C90, C102). OpenEval emphasizes pre-registration as 'gold standard' and notes nearly identical performance on prospective vs retrospective data. Peer reviewers explicitly praised 'inclusion of an independent prospective validation study' as strengthening credibility. Full alignment with SUPPORTED status.

Both address error distribution and comparative performance (C7-C8, C47-C51, C81). OpenEval focuses on error analysis from Figure 3 and lack of item-specific bias. Peer reviewers accepted these as part of overall performance validation, noting 'exceptional accuracy' and 'less degree of error/score dispersion than clinicians.' Both SUPPORTED with full alignment.

Both address explainability and item-level predictions (C9, C79). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED by multihead architecture and interface. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'detailed analysis of individual figure elements' but noting 'explainability could be strengthened' and requesting 'future work to test robustness.' Key disagreement: OpenEval accepts current explainability, peer reviewers want more.

Both address generalization across demographics and conditions (C55, C74-C75). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with minor note that distorted drawing claim is somewhat inferential. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, accepting 'comprehensive data collection' but raising concerns about 'lack of detailed analysis across different patient demographics.' Disagreement on depth of demographic validation.

Both strongly support robustness analysis claims (C76, C121-C123). OpenEval emphasizes systematic testing across transformation types. Peer reviewers explicitly praised 'robustness analysis efficacy' and 'meticulous examination' ensuring 'consistent performance across different clinical imaging scenarios.' Full alignment with SUPPORTED status.

Both support convergence analysis and dataset sufficiency claims (C46, C86, C91-C94). OpenEval notes performance plateau around 8,000-10,000 images and finds speculation about future improvements reasonable. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted through overall positive assessment of methodology. Both SUPPORTED with full alignment.

Both support score-specific performance analysis (C52-C54). OpenEval finds explanations for better performance on high scores logical and well-reasoned. Peer reviewers did not challenge these claims, accepting them as part of comprehensive evaluation. Both SUPPORTED with full alignment.

Both address model architecture and training methodology. OpenEval comprehensively evaluates architectural details and training procedures (C104-C117) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address subset of architecture claims (C104-C106) combined with performance claims, recognizing 'sophisticated application of current AI technologies.' Partial overlap, both SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates augmentation strategies (C107-C108, C118-C120) as SUPPORTED, noting DA transformations are appropriate and TTA approach well-justified. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific augmentation methodology claims.

Both support image resolution analysis (C124-C126). OpenEval finds systematic testing provides empirical justification for chosen resolution. Peer reviewers accepted this methodological detail without challenge as part of rigorous methodology. Both SUPPORTED with full alignment.

Both support practical implementation and deployment (C77-C78). OpenEval notes application interface and beta testing status appropriately stated. Peer reviewers accepted application development, noting 'far-reaching implications for current clinical practice' while requesting more access information. Both SUPPORTED with full alignment.

Both address clinical context and motivation. OpenEval evaluates broad clinical background (C1-C24) as SUPPORTED by established literature. Peer reviewers address subset focusing on manual scoring limitations (C3, C23-C24, C56-C58), accepting motivation without challenge. Partial overlap, both SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates prior work summary (C25-C29) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and critical assessment of previous automation attempts. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these literature review claims.

Both address problems with manual scoring. OpenEval evaluates articulation of manual scoring problems and automation benefits (C56-C61) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address subset (C56-C58) combined with C3, C23-C24, accepting characterization of manual scoring limitations. Partial overlap, both SUPPORTED.

Both address benefits of automation. OpenEval evaluates C56-C61 together. Peer reviewers separately evaluate automation benefits (C59-C61, C80, C82) as SUPPORTED, explicitly recognizing 'significant step forward' and system 'sufficient for clinical use.' Partial overlap on C59-C61, both SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates general deep learning and healthcare data context (C62-C63, C65-C68) as SUPPORTED, representing established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these background claims.

Both support broader generalizability claims (C73, C82-C83). OpenEval finds these reasonable inferences though somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers explicitly recognized broader implications, stating work 'opens avenues for future research' and is 'innovative with implications beyond a single subfield.' Both SUPPORTED with full alignment.

Both address reproducibility and scalability (C80). OpenEval finds this logical inference from automated nature. Peer reviewers include C80 with other automation benefits (C59-C61, C82), accepting reproducibility as inherent advantage. Both SUPPORTED with full alignment.

OpenEval evaluates ethical compliance documentation (C87-C88) as SUPPORTED, noting proper regulatory approvals essential for human subjects research. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these ethical approval claims.
